== Biography ==
'''William James Glasgow''' was born about 1836 in County Antrim, Ireland. On 3 June 1847 an eleven-year-old William James Glasgow of Glenleslie entered Ballymena Workhouse with Mary, Boyd, Mary Jane and Margaret Glasgow.<ref name="Workhouse1847">[https://www.billmacafee.com/otherrecords/ballymenaworkhouse.pdf William Macafee, "Admissions to Ballymena Workhouse: 13th May to 8th July 1847"], registrations 4406–4410 (accessed 13 August 2026).</ref>

The 1851 Ballycregagh return calls William James the fourteen-year-old son of [[Glasgow-2981|James Glasgow]]. He was attending school and was temporarily absent elsewhere in County Antrim.<ref name="Census1851">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy parish, Ballycraigargh, household 29, James Glasgow household: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G94X-YD22 living household, image 251] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L94X-Y621 continuation and mortality return, image 252].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2981]] is assessed at 99% (proved). The held 1851 return calls William James, fourteen, James’s son, temporarily absent at school elsewhere in County Antrim. His 1847 workhouse age eleven and Glenleslie family group support the same childhood identity, regardless of the unproved later 1891 death match.

Held 1851 census relationship quotation/summary and existing source citations establish the census-defined child’s father; no fresh image inspection or adult identity extension.

Next useful test: Inspect the census relationship line and later marriage for the adult bridge.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G94X-YD22 1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy parish, Ballycraigargh, household 29, James Glasgow household: living household, image 251 (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G94X-YD22) and continuation and mortality return, image 252 (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L94X-Y621).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



=== Parentage ===

The census directly proves James as William James's father. [[Hamilton-25516|Peggy Hamilton]] remains attached as an uncertain working mother because no better-supported replacement profile has been identified. Peggy and James reported marrying in 1848, long after William James's birth, so Peggy should not be treated as his proved mother. The marriage year alone does not make earlier biological maternity impossible. Mary of the 1847 workhouse group is the stronger candidate, but no direct maternity record has been found.

The County Antrim birthplace is retained as an uncertain family-locality estimate. The records place William James at Glenleslie and Ballycregagh but do not directly state his birthplace.

The [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/census-record/#census_year=1851&surname__icontains=Glasgow&county=Antrim&limit=30&id=27847 National Archives of Ireland household link] is preserved. [[Glasgow-1694|William Glasgow]], born about 1837, remains a similar-age profile; no record inspected here establishes a duplicate identity.

William Glasgow, aged 58, was indexed as dying in the Ballymena registration district on 30 January 1891.<ref name="DeathIndex18912983">[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death General Register Office for Northern Ireland, civil death index], William Glasgow, 30 January 1891, Ballymena registration district, D/1891/24/1004/7/198.</ref>
